title: Granting a Point, Then Answering It

sections.content: You know *ahora bien* and *no obstante* from B2 Unit 30, *si bien* from B2 Unit 8 and *sin embargo* from B1 Unit 1. In a formal argument you first grant something to the other side, then say what really matters. This lesson adds two phrases for that.

*Si bien es cierto que…* is *si bien* made stronger: "it is true that…, but…". The verb after it is in the indicative. *Cabe señalar que…* means "it is worth noting that…" and adds a point the reader should keep in mind. *Cabe* is a fixed form: it is always followed by an infinitive (*señalar*) and *que*. You know *señalar* from B2 Unit 18.

sections.title: Grant, limit, conclude
rows: Si bien es cierto que el plan es caro, ofrece muchas ventajas.
It is true that the plan is expensive, but it offers many advantages.
El plan es bueno. Ahora bien, cuesta mucho dinero.
The plan is good. That said, it costs a lot of money.
Los precios subieron; no obstante, las ventas no bajaron.
Prices rose; nevertheless, sales did not fall.
Cabe señalar que el plan todavía no está aprobado.
It is worth noting that the plan is not yet approved.

sections.content: A short argument has three moves: grant a point (*si bien es cierto que…*), limit it (*ahora bien…*, *no obstante…*), then conclude. Do not stack them: one concession and one limit are enough, and *cabe señalar que…* belongs where you add a new fact, not where you contrast.
